claim: The Dent du Chat loop from Bourdeau is 14.7 km with 1,100 m elevation gain, ~7h20, rated Very Difficult, topping out at 1,458 m with panoramic Lac du Bourget views.
quote: Distance: 14.7 km / Elevation Gain: 1,100 m / Duration: 7 hours 20 minutes / Difficulty: Very difficult / Maximum Altitude: 1,458 m — magnificent panoramic view of the Lac du Bourget and the Alps.

claim: From La Chapelle-du-Mont-du-Chat the Dent du Chat + Roc de Cornillon route is shorter at ~6.8 km with +830 m, ~4h20, but still rated Difficult with cable/ladder sections unsuitable for those afraid of heights.
quote: The Dent du Chat and the Roc de Cornillon — Distance: 4.25 miles / Elevation gain: +2,720 ft / Duration: 4 hours 20 minutes / Difficulty: Difficult / Those who are afraid of heights may be affected by some technical sections equipped with cables or ladders.

claim: From the Relais du Mont du Chat car park, the Molard Noir out-and-back is only 2.76 km with 113 m gain in about 1 hour, rated Very Easy — the easiest way to bag a Mont du Chat ridge viewpoint.
quote: Distance: 2.76 km / Elevation Gain: 113 m / Duration: 1 hour / Difficulty: Très facile (Very Easy) — out-and-back hiking route that connects two scenic viewpoints: the Relais du Mont du Chat and Molard Noir.

claim: Molard Noir (1,452 m) is actually higher than Dent du Chat (1,390 m) and from its plateau opens a 360° panorama including Lac du Bourget, Aravis, Mont Blanc, Bauges, Vanoise, Belledonne and Chartreuse.
quote: From the small summit plateau, the view opens dramatically onto a 360° panorama including the Savoyard foothills, Lake Bourget, the Aravis, Mont Blanc, Bauges, Beaufortain, Vanoise, Lauzière, Belledonne, and Chartreuse when weather permits.

claim: La Chambotte belvedere at Saint-Germain-la-Chambotte is reached via stairs to a rooftop terrace, free, open year-round, with 360° views of the full Lac du Bourget and the Abbaye d'Hautecombe.
quote: 360° views over the Alps and surrounding area — visitors can see the Lac du Bourget, (the largest natural lake in France), in its entirety, as well as the Abbaye d'Hautecombe. Open all year round / Free of charge.

claim: La Chambotte sits at 725 m altitude, accessible by car with parking nearby, and is one of the postcard panoramas of the Lac du Bourget — Queen Victoria visited in 1887.
quote: At 725 m altitude, the Belvedere de la Chambotte offers you an exceptional 360° panorama of Lake Bourget — accessible by car, with a small parking nearby.

claim: The Grand Colombier (1,531 m, highest point of Bugey) has 11 marked trails of varying difficulty (2 very difficult, 3 hard, 5 medium), with ridge paths offering views of Mont Blanc, Lac du Bourget, the Rhône and Bugey.
quote: The Grand Colombier, the highest point of Bugey (1,531 m)... 11 marked hiking trails... Very difficult: 2, Hard: 3, Medium: 5, Quite difficult: 1 — The ridge trails promise a panoramic view of the Alps, Mont Blanc, Lake Bourget, the Rhone and Bugey.

claim: The full Grand Colombier loop from Culoz station is a serious sportive day: ~32.8 km with 1,600 m elevation gain over ~9 hours — long rather than technical.
quote: Distance: 32.8 km (round trip) / Elevation Gain: 1600m / Duration: 9 hours / Aucune difficulté hormis la longueur du parcours et les 1600m de dénivelé.

claim: From the Grand Colombier summit-parking lot, a 20-minute round-trip walk reaches the orientation table — the lazy option for the same panorama after driving up.
quote: From the parking lot at the top, it is possible to make a round trip of about twenty minutes to the orientation table, and several hikes of a few hours are also possible on the crests.

claim: The Boucle autour de Jongieux vineyard loop is ~10.6 km with +337 m, around 4 hours, rated Moderate, mixing vineyard and forest sections — well-suited as a digestive day-after walk through the Cru.
quote: Distance: 6.60 miles / Elevation Gain: +1,106 feet / Duration: Approximately 4 hours / Difficulty: Moderate — a pleasant, varied walk, with sections through vineyards, others through forest.

claim: Mont de la Charvaz (1,158 m) loop from Billième is ~8.4 km / +650 m / 4h, Medium difficulty, with a steep west-face ascent leading to twin viewpoints over the vineyard, Rhône canal, Bugey and Alps.
quote: Distance: Approximately 8.4 km / Elevation Gain: 650 meters / Duration: 4 hours / Difficulty: Medium — interesting vantage point over a portion of the Alps, the Bugey region, and the Avant-Pays Savoyard.

claim: Mont Tournier (877 m) loop is 10.95 km / +366 m / ~4h10 Moderate, with the Belvédère des Fils clifftop overlook of the canalised Rhône — no railings, not for kids/dogs.
quote: Distance: 10.95 km / Elevation Gain: +366 m / Duration: 4 hours 10 minutes / Difficulty: Moderate — Belvédère des Fils ... dramatic clifftop, though hikers should note the absence of safety railings.

claim: Mont Granier (1,933 m) from Entremont-le-Vieux is a serious 12 km / +1,100 m / 6h sporting hike with the technical Pas des Barres cabled section and the Balme à Colon cave tunnel — open May–November only.
quote: 1,100 meters of positive elevation gain, 12 kilometers, and 6 hours of hiking ... a technical section called Pas des Barres, where you must use cables and iron bars to pass through ... officially open from May 1 to November 30.
